toc.title: Projects Compared with Other Context Tools

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation

  • What a Project is and what it contains
  • How to write effective project instructions (system-level instructions)
  • How to choose and organize knowledge
  • How RAG extends a Project's capacity
  • How Projects differ from account instructions, memory and Skills

2What a Project Is

Running case

Cedarbrook's Customer-Care Project

  • Customer care creates a Project named "Care Replies"
  • Its instructions set the brand voice, the escalation rules and the refund policy summary
  • Its knowledge holds the returns policy, product FAQs and approved reply examples
  • Every agent who opens a chat in the Project gets the same background, with no pasting

A Project is a self-contained workspace with its own chat history, instructions and knowledge base. Everything in it is available to every chat inside it.

Part What it is Typical content
Project instructions Standing guidance applied to all chats in the Project Role, audience, tone, format, rules, how to handle uncertainty
Knowledge Uploaded files and text Claude can use as background Policies, FAQs, product sheets, style guides, templates, examples
Chats Conversations that inherit the above Daily tasks
Project memory Memory kept for this Project only Learned preferences of this work
  • Projects are available to all users, including free accounts, with a limit of five Projects on free plans [Verify live].
  • Why use a Project: consistency, no re-pasting, shared context for a team, and less usage because project content is cached and reused.
  • Team and Enterprise: Projects can be shared with specific people or the organization. Can view = see contents and chat but not edit; Can edit = change instructions and knowledge and manage members. Owners can turn sharing off.
Exam tip

If the same background is needed again and again, the answer is a Project (instructions plus knowledge), not longer prompts.

3Writing Effective Instructions

Project instructions work like a briefing for a new colleague who starts every chat with no memory. They are the "system-level" layer: they apply before your message.

Part What to write Example
Role and purpose Who Claude is here and for what "You help Cedarbrook customer-care agents draft replies to customers"
Audience Who reads the output "Customers aged 25 to 65, non-technical"
Tone and style Voice with a short example "Warm, direct, no jargon; see example replies in knowledge"
Format Structure and length "Under 120 words; greeting, answer, next step"
Rules Must and must not "Never promise refunds over $200; never share other customers' data"
Source of truth Where facts come from "Use the returns policy file; if it is silent, say so"
Uncertainty What to do when unsure "Say you are not sure and recommend a supervisor"
Escalation When to hand over "Complaints about safety go to a manager immediately"
Examples One or two good outputs "See the three approved replies in knowledge"

Good practice

  • Be specific and explain why ("Keep replies short because agents read them on a phone")
  • Use clear sections or bullet points, not one long paragraph
  • Keep instructions short and focused: long instructions use up context; put task-specific instructions in the chat instead
  • State what Claude should do when information is missing
  • Test with real examples, including awkward ones; revise after seeing results
  • Version and date the instructions and name an owner (Module 12)
  • Do not place sensitive data, passwords or personal details in instructions or knowledge unless policy allows it (Module 13)
Exam tip

Strong instructions state role, audience, format, rules, source of truth, uncertainty behavior and escalation. A one-line "be helpful" is a weak answer.

4Choosing and Organizing Knowledge

  • Upload what Claude needs repeatedly: policies, FAQs, product sheets, style guides, templates, examples of good outputs.
  • Quality over quantity. Out-of-date, duplicated or contradictory files confuse answers. Remove files you no longer need.
  • Use clear, descriptive filenames (for example, Returns-Policy-current.pdf) and group related documents in the same Project.
  • Reference documents by name in your questions: "According to the Returns Policy, ..."
  • Limits: project files are limited to about 30 MB each, with text extracted (except for PDFs that include visuals). Total content must fit the context window unless RAG is on [Verify live].
  • Google Docs from Drive can be added to a Project and stay in sync (private Projects) (Module 12).
  • Files in the Project are cached; reuse costs less usage. Caches expire after inactivity.

Retrieval augmented generation (RAG)

Feature Detail
What it does When knowledge nears the context limit, Claude retrieves only the relevant parts with a project knowledge search tool instead of loading everything
Capacity Up to about 10 times more content
Availability Paid plans; automatic; shown by an indicator
Control You cannot switch it manually; Claude uses in-context processing when possible
Quality Designed to keep response quality and speed
Best practices Upload relevant content upfront, clear filenames, related documents together, reference documents by name

5Projects Compared with Other Context Tools

Tool Scope Best for
Instructions for Claude (account) All your chats Personal preferences: your role, tone, formats
Project instructions and knowledge Chats inside that Project A body of work with shared background
Memory Learned across chats (separate per Project) Continuity; not for must-have rules
Skills Loaded only when relevant A repeatable method or format (Module 12)
Styles The tone and format of replies Writing style
Exam tip

Put standing context in the Project and keep the instructions short and specific; move one-off details into the chat.

6Exam Q&A

S1Customer care agents paste the same policy summary into every chat. What is the best fix?

  • ACreate a Project with the policy in knowledge and the rules in instructions
  • BEmail the policy to Claude
  • CUse a shorter policy
  • DKeep pasting it
Show the answer

Answer: A. A Project provides standing instructions and knowledge to every chat.

S2Which Project instruction is most effective?

  • AYou draft replies for Cedarbrook agents in a warm, direct tone, under 120 words, using the Returns Policy file; if it does not cover a point, say so.
  • BAnswer every question that customers ask, in as much detail as possible, and never tell them that you are unsure or that something is not covered by the policy.
  • C"Be helpful."
  • D"Never refuse anything."
Show the answer

Answer: A. It states role, tone, format, source of truth and uncertainty behavior.

S3A Project contains an outdated 2023 policy next to the current one, and answers sometimes contradict each other. What should the owner do?

  • ATell Claude to ignore all of the policies and answer from general knowledge instead
  • BAdd a third copy of the policy file so that Claude has more versions to choose from
  • CDelete the Project
  • DRemove or replace the outdated file and keep clear, current filenames
Show the answer

Answer: D. Out-of-date or conflicting knowledge produces inconsistent answers, so the owner should keep only the current, clearly named version.

S4A Project's knowledge is large and nears the context limit. On a paid plan, what happens?

  • AUploads stop permanently and the Project can no longer accept any new files, instructions or members at all
  • BRAG can turn on automatically, retrieving only the relevant parts and holding up to about 10 times more
  • CThe Project closes
  • DClaude deletes files
Show the answer

Answer: B. Retrieval augmented generation turns on automatically on paid plans and retrieves only the relevant parts, extending capacity by about ten times.

S5Which statement about project instructions versus account instructions is correct?

  • AAccount instructions only work in Projects
  • BProject instructions apply to every chat in your account, and account instructions apply only inside Projects
  • CThey are identical
  • DProject instructions apply to chats inside that Project; account instructions apply to all your chats
Show the answer

Answer: D. Account instructions apply to all your chats, while project instructions apply only inside that Project, so scope is the difference.

S6Which TWO should NOT be stored in Project instructions or knowledge without approval? Select TWO.

  • ABrand tone guidelines
  • BCustomer personal data covered by privacy policy
  • CApproved reply examples
  • DReturn policy summary
  • EPasswords or API keys
Show the answer

Answer: B, E. Personal data and secrets do not belong there unless policy explicitly allows it.

S7A teammate with "Can view" access to a shared Project tries to change the instructions. What happens?

  • AThey cannot; "Can edit" access is needed to modify instructions and knowledge
  • BThey can edit freely
  • CThe Project is deleted
  • DInstructions are changed automatically
Show the answer

Answer: A. Can view lets people read and chat, not edit.

S8Why keep Project instructions short and move task-specific details into the chat?

  • AClaude dislikes long text and will stop reading instructions after a few lines
  • BInstructions are ignored when they have headings or bullet points in them
  • CChats cannot be long
  • DLong instructions use up context and can crowd out the task
Show the answer

Answer: D. Concise, focused instructions save context and usage, while task-specific details can be given in the chat where they are needed.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Project Workspace with instructions, knowledge, chats and its own memory
Free plan Up to five Projects
Instructions Role · audience · tone · format · rules · source of truth · uncertainty · escalation · examples
Style of instructions Specific, explain why, sectioned, short; test and revise
Knowledge Current, clean, clearly named, grouped; remove stale files; about 30 MB per file
RAG Automatic on paid plans near the limit; up to about 10x; retrieves relevant parts
Sharing Team and Enterprise: Can view vs Can edit
Do not store Sensitive personal data or secrets unless policy allows
Compare Account instructions (all chats) · Project (inside) · memory (learned) · Skills (when relevant)
